mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost-push inflation, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential contraction in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline YoY for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline YoY for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, which typically boosts earnings and supports higher equity valuations, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average by >2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which erodes real purchasing power and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month signals a significant labor market shock, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative following a monthly PAYEMS decline of >100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their 6-month averages indicates households are saving more while facing higher prices, which typically reduces consumption and corporate revenues, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 6-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 6-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent deceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and reduced corporate earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.
